title: The Pixel That Differed: Comparing Two Chart Images With a Tolerance and a Count

questions.question: Two renderings of a chart look the same and differ in 150 pixels by at most 16 of 255. What does an exact comparison say?
questions.explanation: That is why a tolerance is needed.

questions.question: What is wrong with a tolerance of 255?
options: No channel can differ by more than 255, so it sees nothing
questions.explanation: At 255 the one red pixel was not found.

questions.question: What does bounds give?
options: The smallest rectangle holding every differing pixel
questions.explanation: Two pixels far apart gave a rectangle holding both.

questions.question: Images of 100 by 50 and 100 by 51 are both white. Do they match?
options: No: a size mismatch, at any tolerance or count
questions.explanation: Comparing the pixels they share would call them equal.

questions.question: Why does compare use QImage::pixel?
options: It reads any format as the same colour value, so formats need not match
questions.explanation: ARGB32, RGB32, premultiplied and RGBA8888 gave 0 differences.

questions.question: A chart moved by one pixel differs in 170. Which guard catches it?
questions.explanation: Stray pixels pass a count of 5; 170 does not.
